summary.problem: When activating custom skills, Gemini CLI aggressively scans .venv directories and fails to respect .gitignore or .geminiignore rules located within the skill directory.
summary.root_cause: ActivateSkillToolInvocation in packages/core/src/tools/activate-skill.ts calls getFolderStructure(path.dirname(skillLocation)) without passing a FileDiscoveryService initialized for the skill directory, causing local ignore rules to be bypassed. Furthermore, .venv is missing from DEFAULT_IGNORED_FOLDERS in packages/core/src/utils/getFolderStructure.ts.
summary.context: Custom skills located in ~/.gemini/skills/ or .gemini/skills/ that contain Python virtual environments (.venv) flood the LLM context with thousands of library files up to the 200-item limit, wasting tokens and obscuring real source files.

steps: Add '.venv' to DEFAULT_IGNORED_FOLDERS in packages/core/src/utils/getFolderStructure.ts to ensure virtual environment directories are ignored by default.

In packages/core/src/tools/activate-skill.ts, update getOrFetchFolderStructure to create a FileDiscoveryService instance for the skill directory (path.dirname(skillLocation)) and pass it as { fileService } in the options argument to getFolderStructure.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When generating folder structure for a directory or custom skill, .venv directories are ignored by default, and local .gitignore and .geminiignore files in the skill directory are respected.
verification_steps: Add unit tests in getFolderStructure.test.ts verifying that .venv is included in default ignored folders and marked with '...'.

Add unit tests in getFolderStructure.test.ts verifying that when a FileDiscoveryService is provided for a skill directory, files and subdirectories matching .gitignore or .geminiignore inside that directory are excluded from the output.

github_metadata.title: GEMINI CLI aggressively scans .venv in custom skills (ignores .gitignore / .geminiignore)
